findings.title: 8/48 internal links are broken (16.7%)
findings.evidence: Checked 48 unique internal link targets; 8 returned HTTP 4xx/5xx. Sample broken URLs: https://www.allbirds.com/collections/womens-sandals (HTTP 0); https://www.allbirds.com/collections/best-for-traveling-mens (HTTP 0); https://www.allbirds.com/collections/shop-all-26 (HTTP 0); https://www.allbirds.com/collections/womens-spring-colors (HTTP 0); https://www.allbirds.com/collections/mens-terralux-cl (HTTP 0); https://www.allbirds.com/collections/mens-bestsellers (HTTP 0); https://www.allbirds.com/products/womens-dasher-nz-blizzard-deep-navy (HTTP 0); https://www.allbirds.com/collections/womens-apparel (HTTP 0).

suggested_action.summary: Implement 301 redirects or update href attributes for broken targets, populated from your server routing table or CMS content editor, because broken internal links dead-end AI crawler discovery loops and destroy conversion when referred visitors land on HTTP 404 pages. Verify: curl -sI <broken_url> returns HTTP 200 or 301.

findings.mechanism: Broken internal links strand visitors referred by AI assistants and waste crawler traversal budget.

findings.title: No Organization JSON-LD found on any crawled page
findings.evidence: Crawled 12 pages. No JSON-LD with @type Organization, LocalBusiness, or equivalent was found. AI assistants use Organization markup as the primary entity anchor for a brand.

suggested_action.summary: Embed Organization JSON-LD inside the homepage head, populated from corporate identity records including name, legalName, url, logo, description, and sameAs, because AI agents inspect root structured data to anchor brand knowledge graph nodes. Verify: curl -s <url> | grep -i '"@type":\s*"Organization"'.

findings.mechanism: Without root Organization schema, LLM crawlers lack an authoritative entity anchor to resolve brand attributes.

findings.title: No content freshness signals found on any page
findings.evidence: Checked 13 pages. 0 pages contain dateModified, datePublished (JSON-LD), article:modified_time, or og:updated_time (meta tags). AI crawlers cannot determine whether this site's content is current.

suggested_action.summary: Add dateModified and datePublished timestamps to JSON-LD and page meta tags, populated from CMS publication and revision timestamps, because AI search crawlers deprioritize unversioned content during real-time retrieval when freshness cannot be determined. Verify: curl -s <url> | grep -Ei 'dateModified|article:modified_time'.

findings.mechanism: AI search crawlers deprioritize unversioned content during real-time retrieval because they cannot determine whether facts are current.

findings.title: No sameAs links in any JSON-LD block
findings.evidence: Crawled 12 pages including homepage and /about. 0 pages contain a 'sameAs' property in any JSON-LD entity. Without sameAs, AI knowledge graphs cannot confidently link this site to its verified external identity on Wikidata, LinkedIn, or Crunchbase.

suggested_action.summary: Add a sameAs array to Organization JSON-LD on the homepage, populated from official corporate profiles on LinkedIn, Crunchbase, and Wikidata, because LLM knowledge graphs rely on canonical sameAs URIs to disambiguate brands from similarly named entities. Verify: curl -s <url> | grep -o '"sameAs":\s*\[[^\]]*\]'.

findings.mechanism: AI models cannot link the brand to authoritative knowledge graph nodes without canonical sameAs entity identifiers.

findings.title: Product pages detected but no Product JSON-LD found
findings.evidence: URL patterns suggest this site has product pages (paths matching /product/, /shop/, /item/), but no Product schema.org JSON-LD was found on any of them.

suggested_action.summary: Add Product + Offer JSON-LD inside <head> on every product page, populated from server-rendered HTML (not JS-injected) including name, sku, offers.price, offers.priceCurrency, offers.availability, brand, image, because GPTBot and ClaudeBot fetch raw HTML without executing JS making JS-injected schema invisible to them. Verify: curl -A 'GPTBot' <url> | grep -i '"@type":\s*"Product"'.

findings.mechanism: GPTBot and ClaudeBot fetch raw HTML without executing JS, so JS-injected or absent schema is invisible to them.

findings.title: Blog/article pages detected but no Article JSON-LD found
findings.evidence: URL patterns suggest this site has blog or article pages, but no Article or BlogPosting JSON-LD was found. AI assistants rely on Article markup to properly attribute authored content.

suggested_action.summary: Add Article or BlogPosting JSON-LD inside <head> on all blog and article pages, populated from server-rendered editorial metadata including headline, datePublished, dateModified, author, and image, because AI assistants rely on structured Article schema in raw HTML to attribute authorship and evaluate content freshness. Verify: curl -s <url> | grep -i '"@type":\s*"Article"'.

findings.mechanism: AI search assistants rely on Article JSON-LD in initial HTML to attribute authored content and evaluate topical relevance.

findings.title: JSON-LD @context is not schema.org across 7 pages
findings.evidence:
Found JSON-LD blocks where @context is not 'https://schema.org' across 7 pages:
- https://www.allbirds.com/products/womens-tree-runner-nz-medium-grey (context: '(empty string)')
- https://www.allbirds.com/products/womens-cruiser-canvas-port (context: '(empty string)')
- https://www.allbirds.com/products/mens-cruiser-medium-grey (context: '(empty string)')
- https://www.allbirds.com/products/mens-runner-nz-slip-on-mushroom (context: '(empty string)')
- https://www.allbirds.com/products/mens-dasher-nz-anthracite (context: '(empty string)')
- https://www.allbirds.com/products/mens-tree-runner-nz-medium-grey (context: '(empty string)')
- https://www.allbirds.com/products/womens-dasher-nz-blizzard-deep-navy (context: '(empty string)')
Expected '@context': 'https://schema.org'.

suggested_action.summary: Set @context to 'https://schema.org' across all JSON-LD blocks, populated from global schema template constants, because AI parsers require the canonical schema.org context vocabulary to resolve linked data types. Verify: curl -s <url> | grep -o '"@context":\s*"[^"]*"'.

findings.mechanism: AI parsers require the canonical schema.org context URI to interpret semantic types correctly.

findings.title: About page lacks sufficient disambiguating identity facts (score: 2/6)
findings.evidence: About page: https://www.allbirds.com/our-story. Detected disambiguating facts: location hq, industry vertical. Missing categories: founding year, team size, customer count, geographic reach. Generic About pages increase the risk of AI entity confusion.

suggested_action.summary: Expand the About page with concrete entity attributes, populated from corporate records covering founding year, HQ location, executive leadership, and industry classification, because vague marketing copy prevents AI systems from extracting factual entity triples. Verify: curl -s <url>/about | grep -Ei 'founded|headquarter|locations|ceo|leadership'.

findings.mechanism: Abstract marketing text without factual timestamps, locations, or organizational structure prevents LLMs from synthesizing reliable entity profiles.

findings.title: High internal link count (>100 links) — crawl capped at 20 fetches
findings.evidence: Page at https://www.allbirds.com contains 114 internal links (>100 links detected); link fetches were capped at 20 to prevent excessive crawl load.

suggested_action.summary: Review navigation and link architecture on high-link pages, populated from page templates, because dense pages with over 100 links can dilute PageRank and exhaust AI crawler budget. Verify: curl -s https://www.allbirds.com | grep -c '<a '.

findings.mechanism: Pages with over 100 links dilute crawl budget and link equity, causing AI crawlers to truncate discovery before indexing deeper content.

findings.title: Render check inconclusive for 4 pages — possible JS gate or consent wall
findings.evidence:
After consent-banner dismissal and extended waits, 4 page(s) returned rendered text that was less than 20% of the raw-HTML word count. This typically means content is behind a JavaScript gate, cookie-consent paywall, or login wall that automated rendering cannot reliably pass. Render-gap analysis could not run for these pages:
  - https://www.allbirds.com
  - https://www.allbirds.com/products/womens-tree-runner-nz-medium-grey
  - https://www.allbirds.com/collections/mens-mizzles
  - https://www.allbirds.com/collections/mens-sneakers

suggested_action.summary: Render primary content without blocking consent overlays or JS gates, populated from initial server HTML delivery, because AI retrieval crawlers cannot interact with consent dialogs or solve client-side challenges. Verify: curl -s <url> contains primary article text without modal barriers.

findings.mechanism: Mandatory client-side consent gates prevent automated AI agents from reaching actual content.

beyond_problem_suggestions.title: Cross-link verified entity profiles across independent authority platforms via sameAs
beyond_problem_suggestions.rationale: Independent corroboration across Wikipedia, Crunchbase, LinkedIn, and Wikidata validates brand legitimacy and feeds entity resolution algorithms in knowledge graph construction (Appendix D/B).
beyond_problem_suggestions.mechanism: LLM knowledge engines construct high-confidence entity nodes by resolving bidirectional sameAs references across independent high-authority knowledge bases.

beyond_problem_suggestions.title: Publish a canonical facts page with unambiguous declarative plain-text assertions
beyond_problem_suggestions.rationale: A dedicated /facts or /about page presenting one unambiguous plain-text sentence per core attribute (founding date, headquarters, leadership, core products) eliminates extraction ambiguity for LLM crawlers (Appendix C).
beyond_problem_suggestions.mechanism: Declarative single-fact sentences minimize semantic parsing entropy during retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) and prevent hallucinated brand claims.

beyond_problem_suggestions.title: Structure conversational FAQ sections with question-shaped headings matching user prompts
beyond_problem_suggestions.rationale: Formulating headings as explicit natural-language questions directly mirrors user prompt patterns submitted to AI search engines (Appendix B).
beyond_problem_suggestions.mechanism: Question-formatted headings maximize semantic vector cosine similarity against conversational user queries, triggering direct answer citations.

beyond_problem_suggestions.title: Implement hreflang annotations and locale-specific schema for regional disambiguation
beyond_problem_suggestions.rationale: Explicit hreflang link tags and localized schema markup distinguish regional product lines, currencies, and language variations for global AI assistants (Appendix E).
beyond_problem_suggestions.mechanism: Locale and alternate tags prevent search bots from conflating regional entities or surfacing incorrect currency and availability in localized AI answers.

beyond_problem_suggestions.title: Embed machine-readable TL;DR summary blocks at the top of transactional emails
beyond_problem_suggestions.rationale: AI email summarizers (e.g., Apple Intelligence, Gemini in Gmail, Copilot) generate automatic summaries based on early email tokens, requiring key details upfront (Appendix F).
beyond_problem_suggestions.mechanism: Structured key-value summary blocks at the beginning of email HTML ensure client-side AI summarizers extract order numbers, dates, and actions without truncation errors.

beyond_problem_suggestions.title: Maintain accurate <lastmod> timestamps in sitemap.xml to signal content freshness
beyond_problem_suggestions.rationale: Including precise, genuine <lastmod> dates in sitemap.xml enables AI crawlers with limited crawl budgets to discover and ingest fresh updates promptly (Appendix A).
beyond_problem_suggestions.mechanism: AI search engines prioritize re-crawling URLs with recent sitemap <lastmod> timestamps, keeping their retrieval indexes and vector embeddings synchronized.
